name: Goth
description: Slow, fluid and theatrical. The body sways, the arms tell the story, and the floor is never rushed. A lot of goth tracks run at a normal club tempo, but the dancing sits on every other beat. Moving in half time is what gives it that drifting, unhurried look. Danced to Post-punk, Deathrock, Darkwave and Coldwave, usually around 100–140 BPM. Each move card has the cues and a beat to count along to: try it, then mark whether you could do it.

source.name: Written for Study Buddy as a casual primer.

questions.prompt: Half-time drift: how does it go?
answers: Slow, gliding steps on every other beat, as if you were walking through water.
steps: Step slowly to the side, or a little forward, on 1
Let the other foot follow and settle on 2, no rush
Step the other way on 3, settle on 4
Keep the upper body tall and let the head turn slowly with the steps

beat.counts: Step on 1, hold 2 · step on 3, hold 4

questions.explanation: Dancing in half time is what makes goth dancing look effortless, even at a club tempo. Tip: Roll through the whole foot when you step, heel to toe or toe to heel. Tip: Close your eyes for a few bars to stop yourself rushing.
questions.note: Watch out for: stepping on every beat, which turns it into a march.

questions.prompt: Cobweb hands: how does it go?
answers: Hands slowly push and part the air in front of you, as if you were clearing away cobwebs.
steps: Bring both hands up in front of your face, palms out
Over two beats, sweep one hand slowly out and down to the side
Over the next two, the other hand follows on its own path
Let the wrists lead and the fingers trail behind
questions.explanation: Tip: Change levels: high above the head, then low by the hips. Tip: Your eyes can follow one hand, which adds a lot of drama for free.
questions.note: Watch out for: moving both arms the same way at the same time, which looks mechanical.

questions.prompt: Slow turn: how does it go?
answers: A small, unhurried turn on the spot in tiny steps, with the arms trailing.
steps: Turn your head and shoulders a little first to start the turn
Take tiny steps on the spot in that direction, one every two beats
Finish facing the front after 8 beats
Let one arm float out behind you as you turn
questions.explanation: Tip: Pick a spot on the wall and find it again at the end, so you don't get dizzy. Tip: Turn the other way next time, so both sides get practice.
questions.note: Watch out for: spinning on one foot, which is fast and needs much more space.
